status: Window checkpoint snapshot and encoding admission integrated; full acceptance remains open
implementation: Scoped window snapshots reuse snapshotOwnedRows; scoped encoding reuses encodeOwnedCheckpoint and preserves the stable checkpoint byte format.

Spilled run snapshots and encoded buffers use a per-run scope held through the awaited write, then release before the next run. Run-reference records and final checkpoint bytes remain admitted through final consumption.

Checkpoint collection now separates backend result lifetime from input lifetime. Once the generic collector owns detached output, backend records and computed values release before serialization; input rows remain pinned for the snapshot.

Checkpoint writes check cancellation and query counters/time before run work and after awaited writes. A cancellation during either a run write or final manifest write rejects instead of returning success; buffers remain charged until the write settles.

cases: Stable-byte parity for Unicode, escaping, bigint, binary and null snapshots
Measured exact snapshot/encoding peak succeeds and one byte below rejects
Run bytes remain admitted during delayed successful and failed writes
Cancellation during a run write and final checkpoint write rejects and releases reservations
Oversized runs reject before the spill writer is invoked
Existing large computed-window checkpoint verifies 64 KiB rejection and 128 KiB success once JSON encoding overlap is charged
